questions.md:
Let $S = \{a, b, c\}$ and $P(S)$ be the power set of $S$. Draw the Hasse diagram of the poset $(P(S), \subseteq)$. Is it a lattice? Justify your answer.

Also list all the antichains of length more than one in the poset $P(S)$.

i. Verify whether the following lattice is distributive. Justify your answer.

*Lattice diagram: $0$ at the bottom, three incomparable elements $a$, $b$, $c$ in the middle (each covering $0$), $1$ at the top (covering $a$, $b$, $c$) — the diamond lattice $M_3$.*

ii. If a lattice $(A, \le)$ is distributive, then show that for any elements $a, b, c$ in $A$,

$$(a \vee b) \wedge c \le a \vee (b \wedge c)$$

Let

$$E(x_1, x_2, x_3) = \overline{x_1} \vee \overline{\left(\overline{x_2} \vee \left(\overline{x_3} \wedge x_1\right)\right)}$$

be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra $(\{0,1\}, \vee, \wedge, \overline{\phantom{x}})$. Write $E(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ in both disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms.
Determine the number of integers between 1 and 250 (including 1 and 250) that are not divisible by any of the integers 2, 3, 5 and 7.
Show that the number of partitions of $n$ is equal to the number of partitions of $2n$ which have exactly $n$ parts.
Find the $60^{\text{th}}$ permutation of the five marks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in Fike's order.

questions.skill: Subgroup criterion and abelian group proof
questions.md:
i) Prove that a nonempty subset $H$ of a group $(G, *)$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $a * b^{-1} \in H$ for every $a, b \in H$.

ii) Define $*$ on $\mathbb{R} - \{0\}$ as $a * b = \dfrac{ab}{5}$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R} - \{0\}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ is the set of all real numbers. Show that $(\mathbb{R} - \{0\}, *)$ forms an abelian group.

questions.skill: Ramsey-type triangle in graph or complement
questions.md: If $G$ is any graph with 6 vertices, then show that either $G$ or $\bar{G}$ contains a triangle.

questions.skill: Solve linear system by LU decomposition
questions.md:
Solve

$$\begin{aligned} 2x_1 + x_2 - x_3 &= 1 \\ x_1 + 2x_2 + x_3 &= 8 \\ -x_1 + x_2 - x_3 &= -5 \end{aligned}$$

by the LU decomposition method.

questions.skill: Lagrange's theorem and cyclic group check
questions.md:
i. If $G$ is a finite group and $H$ a subgroup of $G$, then show that the order of $H$ divides the order of $G$.

ii. Is the group $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ under the operation "multiplication modulo 7" cyclic? Justify your answer.

questions.skill: Count vertex degrees in a tree
questions.md: In a tree with 14 pendant vertices, the degree of every non-pendant vertex is either 4 or 5. Find the number of vertices of degree 4 and 5, respectively.

Using Dijkstra's algorithm, find the shortest paths from $s$ to all the other vertices.

*Weighted directed graph with vertices s, a, b, c, f, t and edges: $s\to a$ (3), $s\to b$ (4), $a\to c$ (2), $a\to b$ (6), $a\to f$ (7), $b\to f$ (5), $c\to f$ (1), $c\to t$ (8), $f\to t$ (4).*

Find a singular value decomposition of the matrix

$$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$$
Show that $s \vee r$ is tautologically implied by the premises $p \vee q$, $p \to r$, and $q \to s$.

Prove that

$$(\exists x)(D(x) \wedge A(x)),\ (\forall x)(A(x) \to C(x)) \Rightarrow (\exists x)(D(x) \wedge C(x)).$$

Draw the Hasse diagram for the poset $A = \{1, 2, 3, 12, 18, 36\}$ with a partial ordering relation defined as: $a$ is related to $b$ if and only if $a$ divides $b$. Is it a lattice? Justify your answer. Also list all the antichains of length more than one in the poset $A$.

In a Boolean algebra $(A, \vee, \wedge, \overline{\phantom{x}})$, show that

(i) every element has a unique complement.

(ii) $a \vee (\bar{a} \wedge b) = a \vee b$ and $a \wedge (\bar{a} \vee b) = a \wedge b$ for all $a, b \in A$.

Let

$$E(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (\overline{x_1} \wedge x_2 \wedge \overline{x_3}) \vee (x_1 \wedge \overline{x_2}) \vee (x_1 \wedge x_3)$$

over $(\{0,1\}, \vee, \wedge, \overline{\phantom{x}})$ be a Boolean expression. Write $E(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ in both CNF and DNF.

How many ways are there to select a total of 15 items from a collection of three types of items where the selection of each type has the following conditions:

i. Type A selection must be between 1 and 4 items.

ii. Type B selection must be between 3 and 7 items.

iii. Type C selection must be between 5 and 10 items.
Show that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is smaller than 3 is equal to the number of partitions of $n+3$ in which the three largest parts are consecutive integers.
Find the $75^{\text{th}}$ permutation of the five marks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in Fike's order.

questions.skill: Abelian group proof and product subgroup
questions.md:
(i) Prove that the set $D$ of all odd integers forms an abelian group with respect to the binary operation $*$ defined by $a * b = a + b - 1$ for all $a, b \in D$.

(ii) Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$ with $HK = KH$. Then prove that $HK$ is a subgroup of $G$.
Show that if $G$ is a regular self-complementary graph of order $n$, then $n = 4t + 1$ for some integer $t$.

questions.skill: Solve linear system by LU decomposition
questions.md:
Solve

$$\begin{aligned} 2x + y + z &= 5 \\ 3x + 5y + 2z &= 15 \\ 2x + y + 4z &= 8 \end{aligned}$$

by the LU decomposition method.

questions.skill: Prove cyclic and small groups abelian
questions.md:
Prove that

i) Every cyclic group is abelian.

ii) Any group with at most five elements is abelian.
If $G$ has $p$ vertices and minimum degree $\delta(G) \ge \dfrac{p-1}{2}$, then prove that $G$ is connected.

Use Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest paths from $v_1$ to all other vertices for the network given below.

*Weighted directed graph on $v_1,\dots,v_6$ with edges: $v_1\to v_2$ (4), $v_2\to v_1$ (6), $v_1\to v_3$ (5), $v_2\to v_3$ (4), $v_3\to v_2$ (6), $v_2\to v_5$ (8), $v_5\to v_1$ (3), $v_3\to v_4$ (2), $v_3\to v_6$ (3), $v_6\to v_3$ (5), $v_6\to v_4$ (4), $v_5\to v_4$ (2), $v_4\to v_5$ (7).*

Find a singular value decomposition of the matrix

$$\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 11 & 14 \\ 8 & 7 & -2 \end{bmatrix}.$$

Consider the following premises:

- If there was a ball game, then travelling was difficult.
- If they arrived on time, then travelling was not difficult.
- They arrived on time.

Using propositional inference theory, show that there was no ball game.

Show that from the premises

$$(\exists y)\,(M(y) \wedge \neg W(y))$$

and

$$(\exists x)\,(F(x) \wedge S(x)) \to (\forall y)\,(M(y) \to W(y))$$

the conclusion $(\forall x)\,(F(x) \to \neg S(x))$ follows.

questions.skill: Diameter of graph and its complement
questions.md: Show that if the diameter of $G$ is greater than or equal to 3, then the diameter of $\overline{G}$ is less than or equal to 3. Hence show that the diameter of a self-complementary graph is either 2 or 3.

questions.skill: Prove edge count of a tree
questions.md: Show that a tree with $p$ vertices has $p-1$ edges.

i. Let $G$ be a connected graph. Show that if all cycles of $G$ are even, then $G$ is bipartite.

ii. Show that $s \vee r$ is tautologically implied by $(p \vee q) \wedge (p \to r) \wedge (q \to s)$.

In the following network, write the distance matrix and find the shortest distance to the vertices $A, B, D, E$ from $C$ using Dijkstra's Algorithm.

*Directed weighted graph on A, B, C, D, E with edges: C→A (12), C→B (6), B→C (5), A→B (7), A→D (6), D→A (4), D→B (5), B→E (10), C→E (3), E→C (8), D→E (6), E→A (11). See the figure in the paper to confirm arrow directions.*

questions.skill: Inverse of a product in groups
questions.md: Prove that in a group $G$, $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$, $\forall\, x, y \in G$.
Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Show that $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ if and only if $xN = Nx$, $\forall\, x \in G$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$.

i. Show that $H \cap K$ is a subgroup of $G$.

ii. Is $H \cup K$ a subgroup of $G$? Justify.
Show that the proportion of the permutations of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ which contain no consecutive pair $(i, i+1)$ for any $i$ is approximately $\dfrac{n+1}{ne}$.

How many ways are there to distribute eight different toys among four children such that

a) each child gets at least one toy?

b) the first child gets at least two toys?
In a lattice $(A, \le)$, for any elements $a, b, c \in A$, show that if $a \le b$ then $a \vee (b \wedge c) \le b \wedge (a \vee c)$.

Express

$$E(x_1, x_2, x_3) = \overline{\overline{(x_1 \vee x_2)} \vee (\overline{x_1} \wedge x_3)}$$

as a conjunctive normal form and disjunctive normal form over $\langle \{0, 1\}, \vee, \wedge, ^{-} \rangle$.

Find the 50th permutation of the five marks $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ in

1. Reverse lexicographic order.
2. Fike's order.
3. Lexicographic order.

Consider the following premises:

i. If Alex does not study hard, then Alex will not pass the exam or he will not get extra credit.

ii. If Alex does not pass the exam, then Alex will attend summer school.

iii. If Alex does not get extra credit, then Alex will join a study group.

iv. Alex does not attend summer school.

v. Alex does not join a study group.

Using rules of inference, show that Alex studies hard. Justify each step with the inference rule used.
Show that from $(\exists x)[F(x) \wedge S(x)] \to (y)[M(y) \to W(y)]$ and $(\exists y)[M(y) \wedge \neg W(y)]$ the conclusion $(x)[F(x) \to \neg S(x)]$ follows.

a. In a distributive, complemented lattice, prove that if $a \le b$ then $a \wedge \overline{b} = 0$.

b. Check if the lattice given by the following diagram is a distributive lattice.

*Lattice diagram ($M_3$ / diamond): 0 at the bottom, three incomparable elements b, a, c in the middle (each covering 0), 1 at the top covering all three.*
Draw any two self-complementary graphs with 5 vertices and find the diameter of those graphs.
Prove that a graph $G$ is a tree if and only if between every pair of vertices there exists a unique path.

i. Suppose two graphs, $G$ and $H$, are Eulerian. If an arbitrary vertex of $G$ is made adjacent to an arbitrary vertex in $H$, is the new graph Eulerian? Give reason.

ii. Show that $(\neg p \wedge (\neg q \wedge r)) \vee (q \wedge r) \vee (p \wedge r) \Leftrightarrow r$.

Using Dijkstra's algorithm, find the shortest path from $b$ to all other vertices for the network given below.

*Directed weighted graph on a, b, c, f, g, h. Edges as read from the figure: a→c (6), b→c (4), b→a (3), a→b (5), b→h (7), c→f (6), f→c (7), c→h (11), f→a (11), f→g (9), f→h (4), h→f (9), h→g (4), g→h (5), h→a (11), a→g (17). See the figure in the paper to confirm arrow directions.*
Let $G = \mathbb{R} - \{-1\}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ is the set of real numbers). Define $*$ on $G$ as $a * b = a + b + ab$. Then show that $(G, *)$ forms a group. Is $G$ Abelian? Justify your answer.
Show that $Z_5 = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$ forms a cyclic group under the operation addition modulo 5. List all the generators of $Z_5$.
Prove that a nonempty subset $H$ of a group $(G, *)$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $a * b^{-1} \in H$ for every $a, b \in H$.
If repetition is not allowed, how many four-digit numbers can be formed from the digits $1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8$? How many of the numbers are less than 4000?

How many ways are there to distribute 27 identical jellybeans among three children

a) without restrictions?

b) with each child getting at least 5 beans?
For any $a, b, c, d$ in a lattice $(A, \le)$, if $a \le b$ and $c \le d$, then show that $a \vee c \le b \vee d$ and $a \wedge c \le b \wedge d$.

Let

$$E(x_1, x_2, x_3) = \overline{(x_1 \wedge x_2)} \vee \left(\overline{(x_1 \wedge x_3)} \vee x_2\right)$$

be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra. Write $E(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ in both DNF and CNF.

Find the following permutations for $n = 5$ with initial permutation $12345$.

i. 90th permutation in lexicographical order

ii. 90th permutation in reverse lexicographical order

iii. 100th permutation in Fike's order

Consider the following premises:

- If there was a ball game, then travelling was difficult.
- If they arrived on time, then travelling was not difficult.
- They arrived on time.

Using propositional inference theory, show that there was no ball game.
Prove that $(\exists x)(P(x) \wedge Q(x)) \Rightarrow (\exists x)\, P(x) \wedge (\exists x)\, Q(x)$.
Let $(L, \le)$ be a distributive lattice. Prove that for any elements $x, y \in L$, if $a \vee x = a \vee y$ and $a \wedge x = a \wedge y$ for some $a \in L$, then $x = y$.

Consider the complete graph on 8 vertices and the cycle graph with 5 vertices. For each of these graphs, state with justification whether the graph is

i) self-complementary

ii) bipartite.
Prove that a graph is a tree if and only if between every pair of vertices there exists a unique path.

i) Show that for all $n > 3$, the complement of the path graph $P_n$ is connected.

ii) Show that $\neg(P \leftrightarrow Q) \Leftrightarrow (P \leftrightarrow \neg Q)$.

Using Dijkstra's algorithm, find shortest paths from $A$ to all the other vertices in the graph given below.

*Weighted directed graph on A, B, C, D, E: A→B (12), B→A (7), B→C (3), B→D (2), D→B (2), C→D (12), D→C (8), C→A (12, long arc over the top), A→E (5), E→A (3), E→D (3), D→E (10). See the figure in the paper to confirm arrow directions.*

questions.skill: Verify abelian group under multiplication mod 7
questions.md: Show that $(\mathbb{Z}_7 - \{0\}, \times_7)$ forms an abelian group under the operation of multiplication modulo 7.

Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then show that $H$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ if and only if $xH = Hx,\ \forall x \in G$.

Give an example of a normal subgroup of $G$.

questions.skill: Prove subgroups of cyclic groups cyclic
questions.md: Prove that every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic. Illustrate this result with an example.

questions.skill: Count selections of two disjoint groups
questions.md:
Given integers $1, 2, \ldots, 11$. Two groups are made, the first group contains 5 integers and the second group contains 2 integers. In how many ways can the selection be made with no repetition if

i) There are no further restrictions

ii) A group has either only odd integers or only even integers.
In how many ways can 20 identical objects be distributed into 5 distinct boxes such that the first box can have at most 3 objects and the second box can have at most 7 objects?

questions.skill: Prove associativity of join and meet
questions.md: Show that the join and meet operations in a lattice are associative.

questions.skill: Convert Boolean expression to DNF, CNF
questions.md:
Let

$$E(x_1, x_2, x_3) = \overline{\overline{(x_1 \wedge x_2)} \vee (\overline{x_2} \wedge x_3)}$$

be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra. Write $E(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ in both DNF and CNF.

questions.skill: Find nth permutation, lexicographic and Fike
questions.md:
Find the following permutations for $n = 5$ with initial permutation 12345.

i) $97^{\text{th}}$ permutation in lexicographical order

ii) $108^{\text{th}}$ permutation in Fike's order

questions.skill: Derive conclusion using rules of inference
questions.md:
Show that $A 	o 
eg D$ follows logically from the premises $A 	o (B \vee C)$, $B 	o 
eg A$ and $C 	o 
eg D$.
Show that the conclusion $(\exists x)[A(x) \to \neg B(x)]$ follows logically from $(\exists y)[P(y) \wedge \neg Q(y)]$ and $(\forall x)[A(x) \wedge B(x)] \to (\forall y)[P(y) \to Q(y)]$.

questions.skill: Prove De Morgan laws and distributivity duality
questions.md:
i) In a Boolean algebra, for any two elements $a$ and $b$ show that

(a) $\overline{a \vee b} = \overline{a} \wedge \overline{b}$

(b) $\overline{a \wedge b} = \overline{a} \vee \overline{b}$

ii) Prove that if the meet operation is distributive over the join operation in a lattice, then the join operation is distributive over the meet operation.
